title: Permission drift detection and repair playbook for RBAC v2 regression suite
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a detection pipeline and guided repair workflows that identify permission drift between RBAC v2 golden fixtures and actual production/QA state. Integrate results with the existing regression harness so drift is surfaced as test failures with contextual audit log evidence and suggested remediation steps. Correlate SSO/SAML identity mapping changes and admin actions to improve root-cause and reduce false positives.
acceptance_criteria: Scanner runs as part of nightly regression and flags any permission deltas between golden fixtures and live snapshots
Each flagged delta includes at least one correlated audit log entry (action, actor, timestamp) or a note saying no audit evidence found
Regression job annotates the Linear ticket with a compact, human-readable diff and a suggested remediation playbook (one-liner commands or Console UI guide)
Ability to mark a delta as intentional (whitelist) with justification persisted and excluded from future failures until expiration
Integration tests that inject synthetic SSO/SAML mapping changes and verify detection and correlation surface in the pipeline
End-to-end CI job completes within SLAs (nightly job < 90 minutes total, individual scan < 10 minutes for typical spans)
tasks: Design data model for live permission snapshot and canonical fixture hashing
Implement efficient diff algorithm (supporting role inheritance, resource globs, and action aliases)
Wire audit-log fetcher and correlation heuristics (actor similarity, time-windowing, event types)
Add SSO/SAML mapping parser to attribute identity changes to external identity provider events
Extend regression harness to fail builds and post structured run-artifacts (diffs, evidence links)
UI mockup for Console annotation of a detected drift and one-click remediation link
Create whitelist mechanism with TTL and audit trail
Add unit and integration tests plus synthetic SSO change scenarios
Document playbook and runbook for on-call to triage and escalate detected drifts

notes: Why this matters: Drift between intended (fixtures) and actual permissions is a recurring outage risk; surfacing drift with audit evidence reduces MTTI and prevents unauthorized privilege creep.
Risk: High noise if inheritance, templating, or SSO attribute mapping not normalized. Mitigation: canonicalization + synthetic SSO scenarios in tests.
Rollout plan: Start as an opt-in nightly check, then promote to gating on core infra repos after 2 weeks of false-positive rates below threshold.
